open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict” conflicts with “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time” and the `trial_executions` fact, because those executions have newly minted identities each time.
open_points.question: When admission is repeated for the same implementation and unchanged corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict record created for the new TrialExecututions?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and do not create new admission executions
Create a new AdmissionVerdict observation for every admission
Create new TrialExecutions but replace or mutate the existing verdict
open_points.default_guess: Create a new immutable AdmissionVerdict entity for each admission invocation.

open_points.subject: Activation after trial-corpus growth
open_points.text: “the current activation of a contract version is the one recorded last” and admission requires a verdict “over the current corpus,” but the text does not say what happens to an existing activation when a trial case is added and its verdict no longer covers the current corpus.
open_points.question: Does adding or capturing a trial case invalidate, suspend, or leave usable the contract version's existing activation?
options: Leave the existing activation usable
Remove or suspend the activation until readmission
Automatically rerun admission for the active implementation
open_points.default_guess: Leave the existing activation usable until another explicit submission or rollback changes it.

open_points.subject: ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result” conflicts with the stated ability to prove a previously unproven version again after its binding becomes accepted.
open_points.question: Is a ProofResult determined only by `flow_version_id`, or is it a contextual observation that may change as referenced binding statuses change?
options: Immutable result determined only by the flow version
Recomputed contextual result using current binding states
A new persisted proof observation for each proof attempt
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a non-persisted contextual result recomputed from the flow version and current referenced records.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution identity
open_points.text: M23 declares `Identity: value` but says “an attempt's record is issued once”; M07 says an execution observation issued once is an entity and “not a value.”
open_points.question: Is NodeExecution an entity identified by its run/node/map/attempt coordinates, or a content-derived value?
options: Entity identified by execution coordinates
Value identified by all meaning facts
open_points.default_guess: Treat NodeExecution as an entity identified by `run_id`, `node_id`, `map_index`, and `attempt_number`.

open_points.subject: Installation identity and configuration changes
open_points.text: M28 declares Installation a value for which “equal configuration is the same installation,” while also saying its token list is reread so adding or revoking a token takes effect within the installation.
open_points.question: Does a configuration change create a different Installation value, or does one stable installation continue while its live configuration changes?
options: Stable installation entity with changing configuration
New Installation value after every configuration change
No Installation identity; only live configuration snapshots
open_points.default_guess: Use a stable installation entity whose configuration can be reloaded.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution actor
open_points.text: The `try an implementation` action is performed by an agent and K-15 requires actors to be distinguishable, but M07 has no actor or request reference; it contains only `implementation_id`, `trial_case_id`, outcome, outputs, resources and time.
open_points.question: How does a TrialExecution record distinguish an agent-requested trial from an execution created automatically during admission, and which agent requested a manual trial?
options: Add the initiating actor and execution purpose to TrialExecution
Infer automatic trials from AdmissionVerdict links and record an actor only for manual trials
Treat the kernel as actor for every TrialExecution and do not retain the requesting agent
open_points.default_guess: Record both the initiating actor and whether the execution was a manual trial or part of admission.

open_points.subject: Try implementation action
open_points.text: “try an implementation | trial evidence per case” does not state whether the action names one trial case, runs the whole current corpus, or accepts temporary inputs outside the corpus.
open_points.question: Which TrialExecution records does one `try an implementation` action create?
options: One execution for a named existing trial case
One execution for every case in the current corpus
One execution for caller-supplied temporary inputs
Allow both named-case and whole-corpus trials
open_points.default_guess: Run every case in the implementation's current contract-version corpus and create one TrialExecution per case.

open_points.subject: Cancelling a run with an unknown outcome
open_points.text: “a run pending on an unknown outcome continues only on the owner's resolution” and resolution is refused after the run ends, but `cancel a run` refuses only a finished run and says the run ends `cancelled`.
open_points.question: May the owner cancel a run while an EffectAttempt is `unknown`, thereby leaving that outcome permanently unresolved?
options: Allow cancellation and retain the unresolved unknown attempt
Refuse cancellation until every unknown outcome is resolved
Cancel the run but still permit later resolution of its unknown attempts
open_points.default_guess: Allow cancellation because the stated cancel action excludes only already finished runs, and retain the EffectAttempt as `unknown`.

open_points.subject: MCP release action
open_points.text: The primary actions include “release a failed run,” and M19 stores `released_by` and `released_at`, but K-11's “one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`” does not include release.
open_points.question: Is releasing a failed run an MCP product action, and if so which named surface operation performs it?
options: Expose a distinct `release` operation
Include release as a mode of an existing operation
Remove release as a callable product action

open_points.subject: Activation authorization on the MCP surface
open_points.text: K-11 describes “the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel,” while the primary action says an agent may request activation and the kernel activates a proven read-only version, and M09 also permits an authoring agent to roll back a slot.
open_points.question: Which activation requests may agents invoke through MCP: read-only flow activation, function rollback, both, or neither?
options: Agents may request read-only flow activation and authoring agents may request rollback
Agents may request only read-only flow activation
Authoring agents may request only rollback
All activation operations are owner-only
open_points.default_guess: Permit agent-requested read-only flow activation and permit rollback by agents with the author right, as the specific action definitions state.
